summary: Opaque Linux native addon executed on require() harvests browser credentials and cookies with embedded HTTPS exfiltration
details: Package ships only a stripped ~10 MB Linux x64 Rust napi ELF (tools.linux-x64-gnu.node), a one-line README, and a package.json whose main points directly at the ELF. Requiring the package immediately invokes napi_register_module_v1 and runs the native code with the installer's privileges. Extracted strings from the addon evidence browser-credential harvesting (SQLite bindings, 'Found login for ' — the log shape used when iterating Chromium Login Data rows, and 'on Cookie.value when inserting' cookie-store handling) alongside a bundled Rust HTTPS/TLS client (ureq_proto::util, rustls types including CertificateChain, NewSessionTicket, RSA_PKCS1_SHA384, RequireHttpsOnly) and host-fingerprinting primitives (gethostname, getifaddrs, network_adapters, /etc/lsb-release, /dev/disk/by-id/, CPU implementer, bogomips per cpu). No source, repository, homepage, or author is provided; the version string 3.1.40-chrom-381-new-browser-icons-377-1785143176 embeds cover-story tokens and a Unix-timestamp-shaped suffix consistent with automated malicious re-publication. The combination of installer-owned secret-store reads, embedded outbound TLS client, host fingerprinting, and source-less binary-only distribution is the fingerprint of a browser credential/cookie stealer that runs on import.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
